payload.title: The reservation ledger is one file shared by every worktree, and code from before REG-ID throws on any record above 999, so the first ARIA-...-1000 reservation makes `add` fail for every domain in every worktree not yet on the new code, with no rollout note
evidence: tools/gates/finding-registry.ts:189 (the ledger path, join(commonDir, 'finding-id-reservations-v1.json'): one file for every worktree of the clone)
tools/gates/finding-registry.ts:227-262 (loadReservationLedger validates the whole file; the check it replaced was `reservation.sequence > 999`)
tools/gates/finding-registry.ts:733 (loadReservationLedger runs on every allocated add; also :829 add-explicit and :937 narrative import)
docs/reviews/_registry/README.md:18 (the ledger's only description; it says nothing of the sequence width)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md architectural-solution hierarchy tier 4: old code already present in 121 worktrees cannot be made to refuse by construction, so a change to a shared persisted format is documented where its failure is read
payload.notes: Close condition: A rollout note where an operator looks when `add` fails: the ledger entry of docs/reviews/_registry/README.md names the width change, the error older code prints and the cure (merge the branch or main that carries tools/gates/finding-id-grammar.ts). The landing PR of REG-ID repeats it and states that the first four-digit reservation breaks `add` in every worktree not yet on that code.
